name: Legal
summary: Legal AI startups are raising at multibillion-dollar valuations, courts keep sanctioning fabricated citations, copyright rulings on training data are diverging, and AI-specific laws are being delayed or rewritten.

deepDives.title: AI Hallucination Cases Database (Damien Charlotin)
deepDives.why: Daily-updated, searchable list of court decisions worldwide involving AI-fabricated content.

deepDives.title: Hogan Lovells AI Litigation Case Law Tracker
deepDives.why: Structured summaries of AI-related court decisions across key jurisdictions.

deepDives.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Future of Life Institute)
deepDives.why: Full text explorer, implementation timeline and analyses of the EU AI Act.

deepDives.title: LawSites / LawNext (Bob Ambrogi)
deepDives.why: Long-running independent reporting on legal tech products, funding and courts' use of AI.

deepDives.title: Artificial Lawyer
deepDives.why: Trade coverage of legal AI vendors, law firm adoption and deals, with a UK and EU lens.

regions.name: Contract review & drafting
regions.summary: AI platforms for drafting, due diligence and review are used by large firms and in-house teams. Harvey and Legora keep raising at higher valuations while model makers ship their own legal tools.
regions.whyItMatters: Law is one of the clearest tests of whether vertical AI applications can build durable businesses on top of general models.
regions.openQuestion: Will specialist legal platforms hold their ground as general-purpose model providers ship their own legal tools?

landmarks.name: Legora Series E at $8.8B
landmarks.summary: Swedish-founded Legora raised a $550M Series E led by Atreides at an $8.8B post-money valuation. It says the US is now its largest market by revenue.

landmarks.name: Harvey raises $550M at $15.5B
landmarks.summary: Harvey raised $550M co-led by Diffusion and Lightspeed, under six months after a $200M round at $11B. It says 80% of Am Law 100 firms use it.

landmarks.name: Anthropic launches Claude for Legal
landmarks.summary: Anthropic released more than 20 connectors to legal software and 12 practice-area plugins for Claude, a general model provider moving directly into legal work.

landmarks.name: Vals benchmark tests tools against lawyers
landmarks.summary: An independent study of four legal AI tools on seven tasks found at least one tool beat a lawyer baseline on four tasks; lawyers led on redlining and EDGAR research.

deepDives.title: Artificial Lawyer
deepDives.why: Tracks legal AI funding rounds, product launches and law firm rollouts as they happen.

deepDives.title: Vals Legal AI Report
deepDives.why: Independent benchmark of commercial legal AI tools against a lawyer control group.

deepDives.title: CUAD: An Expert-Annotated NLP Dataset for Legal Contract Review
deepDives.why: The standard open dataset for contract clause extraction, used to evaluate review models.

deepDives.title: LegalBench: Measuring Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models
deepDives.why: Collaboratively built benchmark of legal reasoning tasks, widely used to compare models.

regions.name: Legal research & hallucinated citations
regions.summary: AI research tools are common, but fabricated citations in court filings keep growing. A public tracker lists nearly 2,300 decisions worldwide, and sanctions are getting heavier.
regions.whyItMatters: Courts are the most public place where the cost of unverified AI output is being measured and penalised.
regions.openQuestion: Do sanctions and verification rules reduce fabricated filings, or does growing AI use simply outpace them?

landmarks.name: Hallucination case tracker passes 2,200
landmarks.summary: Damien Charlotin's database listed 2,289 decisions involving AI-fabricated content on 10 November 2026, 1,552 from the US. Pro se litigants (1,314) outnumber lawyers (910).

landmarks.name: Three years of handling hallucinations
landmarks.summary: A UNC law library review of how Westlaw and Lexis now flag hallucinated authorities; it counted 1,058 US cases in Charlotin's data, about 60% pro se, by June 2026.

landmarks.name: $145K in sanctions in Q1 2026
landmarks.summary: A ComplexDiscovery tally found US courts imposed at least $145,000 in sanctions over AI-fabricated citations in Q1 2026, including a reported $109,700 tied to Oregon matters.

deepDives.title: AI Hallucination Cases Database (Damien Charlotin)
deepDives.why: The reference dataset: each decision with court, party type, what was fabricated and the outcome.

deepDives.title: Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools
deepDives.why: Stanford study measuring how often commercial legal research tools still hallucinate.

deepDives.title: UNC Law Library: Handling Hallucinations, A Reflection on the Last Three Years
deepDives.why: Law librarian's retrospective on how databases and courts treat hallucinated authority.

deepDives.title: UIC Law Library: Flood of AI-Related Sanctions Persist
deepDives.why: Short guide to recent sanctions orders with pointers to the underlying cases.

regions.name: E-discovery & litigation support
regions.summary: Generative AI document review is being folded into the standard price of major e-discovery platforms, shifting competition from AI add-ons to all-inclusive pricing.
regions.whyItMatters: Document review is a large, measurable legal task where AI is already replacing billable human hours at scale.
regions.openQuestion: Will courts and opposing parties accept generative AI review with the same confidence as earlier predictive coding?

landmarks.name: ILTACON e-discovery AI announcements
landmarks.summary: LawNext's ILTACON 2026 round-up covers AI launches from DISCO, Everlaw, Nuix, Relativity and Reveal, including Everlaw links to Harvey, CoCounsel, Gemini and Copilot.

landmarks.name: Relativity announces claiR assistant
landmarks.summary: Relativity announced claiR, a conversational AI for lawyers, with general availability expected early 2027. aiR for Case Strategy remains a separately priced add-on.

landmarks.name: DISCO all-inclusive AI platform
landmarks.summary: DISCO bundled e-discovery, Cecilia AI, deposition management and timelines into one platform at a single per-GB price on processed data, with no ingest fees.

landmarks.name: Relativity makes aiR standard
landmarks.summary: At Relativity Fest 2025, Relativity said aiR for Review and aiR for Privilege, then paid options, would be included in the core RelativityOne subscription at no extra cost.

deepDives.title: eDiscovery Today by Doug Austin
deepDives.why: Daily practitioner blog on e-discovery case law, vendor news and AI trends.

deepDives.title: EDRM
deepDives.why: Standards body behind the e-discovery reference model, with guidance and working groups on AI.

deepDives.title: DWF: A new era for eDiscovery, reflections from Relativity Fest 2025
deepDives.why: A law firm's view of what bundled generative AI review changes for practitioners.

deepDives.title: ComplexDiscovery
deepDives.why: Analysis of e-discovery markets, pricing and AI governance for litigation support teams.

regions.name: Regulatory compliance
regions.summary: Banks and firms use AI for regulatory change monitoring, KYC and AML, mostly with humans in the loop. US supervisors updated model risk guidance but left generative AI out of scope.
regions.whyItMatters: Regulated industries show how far AI can go where every automated decision must be explainable to a supervisor.
regions.openQuestion: How will supervisors expect banks to validate and govern generative and agentic AI systems?

landmarks.name: FSB sets out sound practices for AI
landmarks.summary: The Financial Stability Board published a final report with 12 sound practices for responsible AI adoption by financial institutions, citing generative and agentic AI.

landmarks.name: US bank regulators issue SR 26-2
landmarks.summary: On 17 April 2026 the Fed, OCC and FDIC replaced 2011 model risk guidance (SR 11-7) with revised guidance that leaves generative and agentic AI out of scope for now.

landmarks.name: Few banks have a defined AI strategy
landmarks.summary: A Wolters Kluwer survey of 148 financial institutions found about 12% call their AI strategy well-defined and resourced, though about 61% are piloting or in production.
landmarks.note: Vendor-run survey; page blocks scripts, figures from search snippet only.

deepDives.title: Federal Reserve SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management
deepDives.why: The primary text of the 2026 interagency guidance that replaced SR 11-7.

deepDives.title: FSB: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of AI, final report
deepDives.why: International reference on how financial institutions are expected to govern AI use.

deepDives.title: CRA: Model Risk Management Guidance SR 26-2 in the Era of AI
deepDives.why: Explains what the new guidance changes and what the generative AI carve-out leaves open.

deepDives.title: Management Solutions: Revised Guide on Model Risk Management
deepDives.why: Technical note summarising the revised interagency model risk guidance.

regions.name: Law of AI (EU AI Act, liability)
regions.summary: The EU has pushed high-risk AI Act obligations back to 2027-2028. In the US, a federal push against state AI laws coincided with Colorado replacing its AI Act before it took effect.
regions.whyItMatters: These rules decide what AI developers and deployers must document, test and disclose, and who is liable when systems fail.
regions.openQuestion: Will US state AI laws survive federal preemption efforts, and will the EU's delayed deadlines hold?

landmarks.name: EU AI Omnibus delays high-risk rules
landmarks.summary: The Council gave final approval to the AI Omnibus, moving standalone high-risk AI Act duties to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded AI to 2 August 2028.
landmarks.note: Exact approval date not stated on page; published as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 in July.

landmarks.name: Colorado replaces its AI Act
landmarks.summary: Governor Polis signed SB 26-189 on 14 May 2026, repealing and reenacting the 2024 AI Act as a narrower automated decision-making law effective 1 January 2027.

landmarks.name: DOJ joins xAI suit over Colorado AI Act
landmarks.summary: xAI sued on 9 April 2026 to block the Colorado AI Act and the DOJ moved to intervene on 24 April. On 27 April the court stayed enforcement under a joint stipulation.
landmarks.note: Case status after the May 2026 replacement law was not confirmed.

landmarks.name: US executive order on state AI laws
landmarks.summary: EO 14365 of 11 December 2025 directed the Attorney General to form an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws. It does not itself preempt any state law.

deepDives.title: EU AI Act implementation timeline (Future of Life Institute)
deepDives.why: Date-by-date list of when each AI Act obligation applies, with links to the articles.

deepDives.title: IAPP US State AI Governance Legislation Tracker
deepDives.why: Tracks cross-sector state AI governance bills that apply to private organisations.

deepDives.title: ETO AGORA: AI governance document archive
deepDives.why: Searchable collection of AI laws and policies with full text and summaries.

deepDives.title: Taylor Wessing: The EU Digital Omnibus on AI, what the political deal means
deepDives.why: Plain explanation of which AI Act deadlines moved, which did not, and what was added.

regions.name: Copyright & training data
regions.summary: Courts are diverging on training with copyrighted works. A record US settlement, a first US appellate ruling, a German loss for OpenAI and a UK win for Stability AI point in different directions.
regions.whyItMatters: The outcome sets what training data costs and whether model makers owe creators licences or damages.
regions.openQuestion: Is training a generative model on lawfully acquired copyrighted works fair use? No US appeals court has yet ruled on that.

landmarks.name: Third Circuit rules in Thomson Reuters v Ross
landmarks.summary: In the first major US appellate ruling on AI training and fair use, the court affirmed that Ross's copying of Westlaw headnotes for a non-generative research tool was not fair use.
landmarks.note: Opinion was issued under seal; details come from news reports.

landmarks.name: Bartz v Anthropic $1.5B settlement approved
landmarks.summary: The court granted final approval on 20 July 2026 to the $1.5B authors' class settlement over pirated books used as training data, first agreed in 2025.

landmarks.name: GEMA v OpenAI in Munich
landmarks.summary: Munich Regional Court held on 11 November 2025 that memorisation of song lyrics in OpenAI's models and their reproduction in ChatGPT outputs infringed copyright.

landmarks.name: Getty v Stability AI in UK High Court
landmarks.summary: The court held Stable Diffusion's model weights are not infringing copies, rejecting Getty's secondary infringement claim, with a limited trade mark win on watermarks.

deepDives.title: CMS Artificial Intelligence and Copyright Case Tracker
deepDives.why: Country-by-country case pages with procedural history and status updates.

deepDives.title: BakerHostetler Case Tracker: AI, Copyrights and Class Actions
deepDives.why: Overviews, status and filings for the US generative AI copyright lawsuits.

deepDives.title: US Copyright Office: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
deepDives.why: The Office's multi-part report, including Part 3 on generative AI training.

deepDives.title: Osler: German and U.K. courts diverge on whether AI models infringe copyright
deepDives.why: Side-by-side comparison of why Munich and London reached different answers on memorisation.

regions.name: Access to justice
regions.summary: Self-represented litigants increasingly use chatbots to draft filings, and a few courts are testing their own AI assistants. Filings are up, but there is little evidence outcomes have improved.
regions.whyItMatters: Most people with legal problems cannot afford a lawyer, so this is where AI could widen access or just add court backlog.
regions.openQuestion: Does AI help unrepresented people win or settle cases, or mainly raise the volume of filings courts must process?

landmarks.name: Courts cope with AI-generated lawsuits
landmarks.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on a rise in AI-drafted pro se lawsuits and on judges weighing what duties apply when chatbots stand in for lawyers.

landmarks.name: Pro se filings rise with AI use
landmarks.summary: A paper by Anand Shah and Joshua Levy finds the pro se share of US federal civil cases rose from about 11% to 16.8% in FY2025; over 18% of sampled 2026 complaints flag as AI text.

landmarks.name: Alaska courts ready AVA probate chatbot
landmarks.summary: After more than a year of work slowed by inaccurate answers in testing, Alaska's courts set a late January 2026 launch for AVA, a probate self-help chatbot built with LawDroid.
landmarks.note: Source predates launch; the court's probate page now links to AVA.

deepDives.title: Shah & Levy: Access to Justice in the Age of AI
deepDives.why: The main empirical study so far, using 4.5 million federal civil cases from FY2005 to FY2026.

deepDives.title: Thomson Reuters Institute: Chatbots for justice
deepDives.why: Explains how court-run chatbots are designed, tested and limited to avoid giving legal advice.

deepDives.title: Cyberjustice Lab: AI as a Gateway to Justice (Beagle Plus and AVA)
deepDives.why: Takeaways from an NCSC webinar on two public-facing legal chatbots and how they were evaluated.

deepDives.title: Stanford Legal Design Lab
deepDives.why: Research group running an AI and access to justice initiative with courts and legal aid.
